heroHeadline: IRGC Announces Hormuz Toll Zone; Trump Launches Escort Mission; Iran Claims Missile Hit US Frigate — Day 66
heroSubtitle: The situation at the Strait of Hormuz reached a new flashpoint on Day 66 (May 4): the IRGC announced a formal maritime control zone across the strait's deep-water channel, claiming authority to charge tolls of over $1 million per vessel and demanding prior authorization for all passage. The announcement followed Trump's May 3 declaration that US forces — 15,000 troops, 100+ aircraft, guided-missile destroyers — would begin 'guiding' commercial ships through Hormuz starting May 5, a mission Iran called a ceasefire violation. Iranian state media then claimed two IRGC missiles struck a US Navy frigate near Jask; the US military immediately and categorically denied any vessel was hit. Iran's 14-point peace proposal, submitted May 2 via Pakistani mediators, was rejected by Trump on the same day as 'not satisfying' — with the nuclear issue still the central obstacle. The IRGC separately warned it would target Israeli power plants and civilian infrastructure supplying US bases if the Hormuz escort mission proceeded. US gas prices hit a new conflict record of $4.45 per gallon on Day 66 — up 49% since the war began February 28. The ceasefire nominally remains in effect, but the Hormuz escort mission's launch on May 5 will test whether either side holds back from direct confrontation in the strait.
